title: Quantization profile onboarding and perf regression tracking pipeline
creator: Sasha Patel
description: Add a repeatable onboarding flow for model quantization profiles (INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ) into the model catalog and wire automated performance-regression detection into CI and the Console. This ticket covers metadata schema, storage of profile artifacts, runtime binding and pinning of quantization variants, CI perf harness, and alerting/backoff behavior when regressions are detected.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Quantization profile schema (metadata + artifact pointer) landed in catalog API and persisted for new and existing models.
2) Runtime can select and pin a quantization profile per model-version and fall back to a safe variant when a perf regression is detected.
3) CI perf harness runs nightly for all onboarded quant profiles and emits regression signals to the Alerting pipeline.
4) Console shows a per-profile performance card (latency/p99/cost delta/quality delta) and a historical regression chart.
5) Automated rollback/fallback policy exists and is exercised in a canary run with traffic shaping.
6) Security review completed for profile artifact storage and access controls.
tasks:
- Design profile schema and minimal required fields (quant_type, bitwidth, calibration_seed, tuning_flags, expected_throughput, expected_latency_percentiles, known-constraints)
- Implement storage API endpoints in model-catalog-service and add DB migration to store profile metadata and S3 pointers
- Extend onboarding CLI to accept quant artifacts (GPTQ/AWQ artifacts + quant metadata) and validate against schema
- Runtime: bind quant profile to model-version at start-up and expose pinning API
- Implement perf-harness: daily CI job that runs a representative prompt set across quant variants and baseline FP16/FP32; calculate regression metrics and thresholds
- Alerting: wire perf-harness outputs into observability pipeline (metrics + anomaly detection) and create Alertmanager rules for perf regressions
- Console: frontend card and drilldown page for quant profile performance + enable per-profile rollout controls
- E2E tests: unit tests for schema validation, integration test for runtime fallback, canary traffic test to validate rollback on regression
- Docs: onboarding guide for model teams, examples for GPTQ/AWQ packaging, and runbook for investigating regressions
technical_notes:
- Profile artifacts for GPTQ/AWQ will be stored as signed bundles in artifacts bucket; catalog stores pointer + signature + created_by + checksum.
- Prefer schema versioning (profile_schema_v) to allow iterative fields.
- Runtime should expose a deterministic order: user_pin -> project_policy_pin -> auto-selected-profile. Auto-selection runs a simple score = latency_weight*latency + cost_weight*cost + quality_penalty*quality_drop.
- Regression detection: use median baseline window (7 days) and require >10% latency increase at p95 or >3% quality drop (per eval metric) to trigger an alert. Thresholds are configurable per-customer.
- For GPTQ/AWQ, include compatibility metadata: supported-sequence-length, kv-cache-format, kernel-hints. Runtime kernel selector will consult kernel-hints to pick optimized path.
- For FP8/INT8, ensure quant calib metadata includes representative-input-spec and random-seed for reproducibility.
- Keep fallback profile as a label: "safe_fallback": "fp16" or specific quant variant. Runtime must gracefully switch with zero-downtime if possible (drain + warm cache).
rollout_plan:
1) Feature flag gating behind 'quant_profiles' feature flag.
2) Internal dogfood: onboard 3 internal models (search-ranking-7B quant variants) and run nightly perf-harness for 2 weeks.
3) Canary: enable for 5% of traffic on a test customer org and monitor regressions for 72h.
4) Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% once no regressions and metrics stable.
5) Monitor and revert via Console rollout controls if automated alerts fire.
